title: The Pragmatic Frames of Spurious Correlations in Machine Learning: Interpreting How and Why They Matter

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative literature review and thematic coding of machine learning publications to analyze how researchers frame spurious correlations that lead to gender bias (e.g., analyzing discussions around Amazon's screening tool, facial attributes in CelebA, and occupational stereotypes in text-to-image models).

Qualitative literature review evaluating how the ML community frames harmful spurious correlations that affect minoritized racial groups, such as performance disparities in autonomous vehicles for darker-skinned pedestrians.
Qualitative literature review examining how ML researchers problematize spurious correlations that cause model failures for minoritized accents in voice recognition systems.

Qualitative literature review analyzing the framing of spurious correlations in toxicity detection models that lead to the over-censorship of LGBTQ+ digital content (e.g., falsely flagging neutral identity markers like 'gay' or 'lesbian' as toxic).
